what: The population key of the twelve filled LEFT sheets of image group 1 (images 1-25), and the pairing of the group's eleven CONTINUATION sheets to them.
parent: T-0539, piece 3 of 3; the ask is T-0535's and before it T-0494's.
why_this_file_exists: A continuation sheet carries no name and no printed page number — its number sits in the corner the binding takes — so nothing on it says which left sheet it continues. Two numbers can say it: the count of ruled lines carrying an entry, which must be the same on both halves of one opening, and the page population, which the left sheet gives as the sum of its 38 printed age-band footings and the right sheet gives as the printed footing of its TOTAL column. This file publishes both keys for every sheet in the group and states the outcome of the test for all eleven continuations.
the_test: A pair must match on BOTH keys. A match on one key alone is recorded as a candidate and refused, with the rule that refused it.

The left key is the enumerator's own printed footings summed across all 38 columns, with a blank footing counted as zero. Where a footing is illegible or disputed the sheet carries two keys and both are published.

The right key is the printed footing of the TOTAL column — the enumerator's own arithmetic over his own sheet — and NEVER a pass's line-by-line sum of that column, which is a second reading and differs on four of the seven sheets that have one.
An unpaired sheet is recorded as unpaired. Nothing here is guessed, and no confidence is raised to make a pairing come out.
what_this_file_does_not_do: It mints nothing, regrades nothing and rewrites no page file's cells. Where the pairing bears on a disputed reading it says so and leaves the residual where the page file recorded it.

continuation_sheets.what_it_settles: 33S7-9YYJ-9K3's disputed column 29. Its footing is two hooked diagonals, read by T-0585 as 11 against 4 in the column's own cells, and the sheet alone could not decide. If the footing were 11 the page would hold 208 persons and the facing continuation foots 201; with the footing read as 4 the two sheets agree exactly. That is a SECOND and INDEPENDENT witness for 4 — and it is the same two-stroke 4/11 form T-0627 and T-0645 settled toward 4 on 33S7-9YYJ-6H. This file does not rewrite the page file: the residual of 7 stays recorded there, with this pairing named beside it.

No left sheet in images 1-25 carries 32 entries — eleven of the twelve are ruled to 31 and the twelfth to 30 — so this sheet's left half is NOT in this image group at all. That is a fact about the deposit rather than a failure of the reading, and it is what the other unpaired sheets below should be read against.

outcome.what_the_result_means: Ten of the eleven continuation sheets in images 1-25 do not pair inside images 1-25, and two of them — 33S7-9YYJ-8D and 33S7-9YYJ-9WS, both at 32 entries — are shown outright to have no possible partner here. The deposit is ordered by sorted filename and not by the book, so a left sheet and its own continuation are only in the same group by accident; the coverage file has said so about the page numbers from the start and this is the measurement of it. The ten are not blocked on more reading of THIS group: they are blocked on the footings of the left sheets in groups 2 and 3, which are read for names but not for cells, and on the three TOTAL footings T-0641 still owns; T-0644's, on 33S7-9YYJ-9WS, is read and is the second sheet ruled out of this group.

outcome.what_the_three_new_footings_do_to_this_g: Nothing, and that is worth stating: 155, 165 and 113 are not the population of any of this group's twelve keyed left sheets, so T-0642's verdict of ten unpaired continuations stands with all eleven footings now read rather than with three of them outstanding. It stands for the reason T-0642 gave — the partners are in the groups whose left sheets have been read for names and not for cells, or outside this deposit altogether. T-0543 also tested all three against printed 232 and refused all three.
